open_points.subject: Randomly minted entity identifiers
open_points.text: “mints `binding_id` (A01 rule 2)” and the flows create TrialExecution, Run, EffectApproval and StandingGrant records whose identifiers M07, M19, M24 and M25 say are “minted at random by the kernel”, but no module owns a randomness source and no capability supplies random bytes or identifiers.
open_points.question: Which module or capability generates and collision-checks the random identifiers used by `functions`, `bindings`, `runs` and `effects`?
options: Each record-owning module uses an operating-system cryptographic random source and checks uniqueness through `store`
`store` owns a transactional random-identifier minting capability
A separate kernel-randomness capability supplies identifiers to the record-owning modules
open_points.default_guess: Have each record-owning module generate a cryptographically random identifier and retry when `store` reports a collision.

open_points.subject: EffectAttempt outcome `not_sent`
open_points.text: State 4 says “The effect sent once ... with its EffectAttempt `applied`, `not_applied`, `not_sent` or `unknown`”, while A09 defines `not_sent` as “nothing could be sent” and an attempt in that outcome as `not_sent`.
open_points.question: Does the State 4 outcome claim that a request was sent when the EffectAttempt is `not_sent`, or is `not_sent` an exception to “The effect sent once”?
options: `not_sent` means no request byte was sent; the outcome sentence needs an exception
Every listed outcome represents a request that was sent, requiring the meaning of `not_sent` to change
open_points.default_guess: Treat `not_sent` as meaning no request byte was sent, following the normative A09 outcome table.
